headline: No documented shared channels or mutable overlaps; pairwise risks are low to none, with only indirect compliance uncertainty from docs-only profiles.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: awesome-prompts is a non-runnable content-writing repo with no I/O surfaces, and risingwave is a separate data-engineering project with no shared channel or ingestion path documented. With no filesystem, clipboard, or MCP bridge shown, there is no plausible default prompt-injection pathway between them.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator copies content from awesome-prompts into risingwave prompts or tools, injection risk appears.
IF a shared filesystem, clipboard, or MCP server is added between them, the pathway changes.
mitigations: Keep the agents isolated with no shared clipboard or workspace.
Do not pipe repo text from awesome-prompts into risingwave tool prompts.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging if a shared channel is introduced.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both profiles show network_egress set to none and data_classes_touched empty, so neither agent is documented to exfiltrate data by default. No shared workspace or authenticated principal is described, so a leakage path is not evidenced for this pair.
conditions: IF either agent is later granted network egress, leakage risk must be re-evaluated.
IF a shared workspace is configured, file-based leakage becomes possible.
mitigations: Keep network egress disabled for both agents.
Avoid placing sensitive files in any shared directory.
Review any future OAuth or API credentials before enabling them.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Neither profile exposes write surfaces, network egress, or concurrency primitives, and both are marked runnable false. Without overlapping mutable resources, there is no documented write-write conflict between awesome-prompts and risingwave.
conditions: IF both agents are deployed with write access to the same directory, conflict risk appears.
IF an orchestrator adds shared locks or mutable state, the assessment changes.
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only in the current setup.
Do not mount a shared writable directory.
requires-engineering: add locking if shared mutable resources are introduced.

D_cascading_error.rationale: awesome-prompts is a prompt/content repository and risingwave is a data-engineering system, but neither profile shows default action-taking authority or a documented pipeline where one consumes the other's outputs as authoritative. The interaction is undocumented, so uncertainty stays low rather than none.
conditions: IF risingwave is configured to execute actions based on text from awesome-prompts, cascading error risk increases.
IF an operator treats repository content as authoritative operational guidance, downstream mistakes can propagate.
mitigations: Require human review before using any generated text operationally.
Do not auto-feed awesome-prompts output into risingwave actions.
Add a verification step before any downstream execution.

E_compliance.rationale: No data classes are documented as touched by either agent, and both profiles show no network egress. With no identified residency, retention, or regulated-data flow, there is no evidenced compliance mismatch specific to this pair.
conditions: IF regulated data is introduced into either agent's workflow, compliance must be reassessed.
IF one agent is deployed under a stricter residency or retention regime, mismatch risk may emerge.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both agents.
Document any future residency or retention requirements before deployment.
requires-engineering: add policy checks if regulated data flows are added.
